2027-02-04.title: Thursday after Aneede Sunday · St John de Britto
readings: I am not ashamed of the gospel
2027-02-04.alt: Season of Denho. Commemoration of St John de Britto, priest and martyr of the Madurai mission (1693).
2027-02-04.verse: For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
theo: Paul writes to a Church he has never visited, and he tells them why he longs to come: “I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish, hence my eagerness to proclaim the gospel to you also who are in Rome.” The gospel is not his property but a debt he owes to everyone. And then the great sentence: “For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith.” In the Gospel Jesus is frank about the cost: “the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it.” The narrow gate is not a door for a chosen few; it is the shape of Christ himself, through whom everyone may enter, but only by leaving behind what does not fit.

Our Church today remembers a man who lived both readings in South India. John de Britto was born in Lisbon in 1647 to a noble family and entered the Society of Jesus. He asked to be sent to the Madurai mission, and from the 1670s he lived among the Tamil people as a pandaram, a poor ascetic teacher, walking barefoot, eating simple food and speaking Tamil. The people called him Arul Anandar. He was arrested and beaten more than once, and was finally beheaded at Oriyur in the Marava country on 4 February 1693, after the conversion of a local chief, Thadiya Thevar, had stirred deep opposition. Pius XII canonized him in 1947. He was a debtor to the poor and to the learned of our land, and he was not ashamed of the gospel.
outline: Ask: when were you last embarrassed to show that you are a Christian?
The gospel is a debt we owe.
The power of God for salvation.
“I am not ashamed of the gospel.”
live: Share one word of faith today with someone who does not know Christ well.
Refuse one easy dishonesty today, even if it costs you.
2027-02-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, you are the narrow gate that leads to life. Through the prayers of St John de Britto, who gave his life for you among the Tamil people, make us unashamed of your gospel, generous to all, and faithful on the hard road that leads to you. Bless the Churches of Tamil Nadu and all who proclaim you in India. Amen.
altar: The martyrs of India offered their lives with Christ; in the Holy Qurbono we offer ours with his one sacrifice.

quick: Paul calls himself a debtor to everyone, wise and simple.
He is not ashamed of the gospel, the power of God for salvation.
St John de Britto lived as a poor Tamil ascetic and died a martyr at Oriyur.

2027-02-04.question: Where am I ashamed of the gospel?

family.explain: St John de Britto came all the way from Portugal to Tamil Nadu. He dressed and ate like the poor people there and told them about Jesus. He was not ashamed of Jesus, even when it cost him his life.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries in India and all over the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a place where we feel shy to pray or to say we are Christians?”

illus: A software engineer from Thiruvalla was sharing a hostel room in Chennai with three colleagues. On the first night he hesitated, then knelt by his bed and made the sign of the cross. Nobody laughed. A week later one of the others asked him, quietly, what he prayed about. That began a friendship that lasted years. He said later: the hardest part was the first ten seconds on my knees.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, give us the courage of your martyrs and make us unashamed of your gospel. Amen.
share: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians (Romans 1:14). To whom do I owe the gospel?
I am not ashamed of the gospel (Romans 1:16). When have I hidden my faith?
The gate is narrow and the road is hard (Matthew 7:14). What easy road am I tempted to take?
pm.resp: Lord, make us bold for your gospel.
interc: For the Church in Tamil Nadu and for the shrine at Oriyur.
For missionaries and catechists in North and South India.
For Christians who are mocked or threatened for their faith.
For students and workers living far from home.
For courage in our own families to pray openly.
pm.close: Father, St John de Britto followed your Son through the narrow gate to martyrdom. Give us his love and his courage, and bring us all to the life that has no end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul writes: I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish (Romans 1:14). The gospel he received is a debt he owes to everyone he meets.
Then he says: I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith (Romans 1:16). Our faith is not a private hobby; it is God's own power.
Jesus does not hide the cost: the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life (Matthew 7:14). We pass through it only by leaving behind what does not fit.

St John de Britto left a noble life in Lisbon, lived as a poor teacher among the Tamil people, and was beheaded at Oriyur in 1693. Let us ask him for courage to pay our debt of the gospel, without shame, wherever we are. Amen.
kids: Children, St John de Britto came from far away Portugal to tell the people of Tamil Nadu about Jesus. He was never ashamed of Jesus. Can you make the sign of the cross before your meal today, even at school?

intro: Theme: “I am not ashamed of the gospel.”
Paul's debt to all, the narrow gate, and a martyr of our own land.

sub: The gospel is not ours to keep.
Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
I am a debtor both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish
points.apply: Pray for one person who does not yet know Christ, and look for a chance to speak.

q: I will also speak of your decrees before kings, and shall not be put to shame;
For I am not ashamed of the gospel; it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who has faith, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross openly before meals this week.

q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
For the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it.
points.apply: Choose one costly right thing today instead of the easy wrong one.

concl: The gospel is a debt we owe to everyone.
The martyrs show that the narrow gate opens on life.
2027-02-04.resolve: Pray this week for the Church in Tamil Nadu and for missionaries in India.
